notes.content: The page names Multomb(F) the grande multiombre, or M-multiombre, and describes it as a set-theoretic figure in M faithfully indexed by the deployment F tilde. Its knowledge is said to imply knowledge of F. The inserted historical sentence says that L had not yet been involved. Restriction along L hooked into M gives inverse-image maps on P and Fig. By composition with 1.6 a)b), display (1.9) assigns F its small shadow omb(F) and small multi-shadow multomb(F). The final text gives the terminology petite ombre, ombre where confusion seems excluded, and (petite) multiombre. No proof or calculation is supplied on this sheet.
math_reading_decisions: The maps in (1.9) are read as live rightward maps with canceled left hooks. The cancellation is retained and does not become a live injectivity assertion.
The first inverse-image line has a full arrowhead; the Fig line has only the upper barb. These literal signs are preserved without assigning different categorical meanings to them.
The manuscript’s doubled F in M-multiombre de F is retained locally. The surrounding prose would naturally refer back to the same figure, but that expectation is not used to remove the doubled stems.

P is the same recurring handwritten token in the inverse-image display and (1.9). Its exact TeX alphabet remains uncertain. The class-domain F is also distinguished from the plain variable F, with its font family left uncertain at the first occurrence.

The sentence about injectivity qualifies the two assignments separately: the first has no reason to be injective; the second has a tendency to be so. This is recorded as a qualified authorial statement, not a theorem checked here.

The t in the b) occurrence of multomb reads as t, but the dense upper strokes leave its previous state unresolved. The clear occurrences elsewhere establish the recurring operator spelling; they do not authorize reconstructing a canceled prior letter.
The reference 1.6 a)b) is transcribed literally. Its prior-page content was not consulted, so composition is checked here only for the visible source/target pattern.
The foot abbreviation is transcribed as barred m, with the semantic expansion même recorded only in the abbreviation table.
author_doubts: “dont la première n’a aucune raison d’être injective, la seconde par contre a une tendance à l’être” — the explicit mathematical qualification on the page.
“quand une confusion semble exclue” — the condition attached to using ombre without petite.
No explicit “vérifier”, “à voir”, proof-check request, or question mark occurs in the visible page. The cross after l’être is preserved without assigning it a conjecture or footnote function.

check_events.outcome: Read the assertion that the grande multiombre is a set-theoretic figure in M indexed faithfully by F tilde and determines F. No proof was present or attempted; no visible formula failure was found.
Checked the restriction direction L into M against P(M) to P(L) and Fig(M) to Fig(L), and the matching codomains in (1.9). The visible compositions parse. The cited 1.6 maps were not inspected.
Inspected the a) arrow’s canceled left end in crop 10 and the b) end in half B. Recorded canceled hooks with live right arrowheads; did not promote them to live injections.
Read and preserved the different injectivity qualifications. No argument establishing injectivity or a counterexample was supplied or claimed.
Crop 03 confirmed doubled F despite the apparent reference back to the same figure. The letter was not silently normalized to plain F.
Crop 11 allowed live t in multomb to be read, but did not separate a definite earlier character from retracing. Explicit uncertainty and comments preserve that limitation.
Crop 14 showed a barred cursive m and the following pour. The expansion même fits the surrounding phrase but is not substituted for the literal sign.
Compared every manuscript line with both supplied drafts, recorded all 12 unique C doubts, retained all observed deletions/insertions, and inventoried the full page. No S rows were supplied.
